title: Lord Cobham (Ostend) to Walsingham, 20-22 March 1587/8, BL Harley MS 287 ff. 70-72 (DECODE R8482-R8487)

steps.what: Fetched the seven page images and the key record R8497 from DECODE with the session cookie.
Checked CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4, March 1588 sections, for these letters.
Compared the Bodley 1590 key R8497 in the same volume.
Cipher runs beside clear words read as 'commaunded to attend', 'that bearer hath', 'instructions', 'under colour thereof', 'any money', fixing most letters.
Read the runs of ff. 70r-72v word by word from context; long runs on f. 70v and 71v read in sense (preparations, eleven companies of footmen, subject to interception).
The cobham1588 session found the same letter values in the contemporary glosses of f. 89 (R8493).

Second pass on full-resolution half-line crops: remaining runs of f. 70r (canal Ghent-Eecloo-Sluys, garrison, victuals), names Pigot and Barney on f. 72r, the last lines of f. 71r; nomenclator signs 15 (Parma) and square (the States) identified from context.
CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4 confirms Captain Barney a prisoner at Ostend and the request for 2 or 3 pinnaces, 22 March 1588.

Reclassified from 'read' (solved) to 'read in part' (solved in part): every run read in sense but the share of cipher tokens read was never measured, and code 42, .7., the Jesuit's surname (f. 71r), one verb (f. 70r) and scattered words stay open. Verification corrected: there is no contemporary decipherment on the leaves; the f. 89 glosses of the sibling letter (R8493) confirm the key values. NOTES gain Remaining gaps and Escalation sections.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): READING.md (readings by DECODE record) and key.tsv; no glyph-level transcription of ff. 70r-72v exists, so the transcriptions point to the DECODE records' images

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): READING.md for 20 March read. R8485 and R8486 build sentences; R8487 holds three short runs with holes. Per-document C overturned to B (the holes are on the short last page); claim unchanged (read in part).

validation.notes: no sign-level transcription in the folder; the reading is word-level only

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The simple substitution was rebuilt from cipher runs read against the surrounding clear English of Cobham's letters ('commaunded to attend', 'that bearer hath', 'instructions', 'any money'); no decipherment or key existed, and the values were later confirmed by the glosses on f. 89 (R8493) in the same volume.
outcome.notes: Every run of ff. 70r-72v read in sense; code 42, .7., one surname, one verb and scattered words open; share read not measured (read in part since 22 Sept 2026). f. 11 (R8477), a different code of about eight groups, not read.

texts.label: R8482-R8483, Lord Cobham to [Walsingham], Ostend, 22 Mar 1587/8 (ff. 70r-v)
texts.summary: Henry Brooke, Lord Cobham, one of Elizabeth's peace commissioners at Ostend in spring 1588, asks that ships be sent to attend on the coast, warns that the garrison is too weak and short of money and victuals, and reports Parma's new ditch from Ghent by Eeclo to Sluys, nearly navigable for his float-boats, and the threat to the town and haven. No sign-level transcription exists: the cipher runs were read word by word from crops of the DECODE images.

texts.label: R8484, intelligence from Middelburg enclosed (f. 71r)
texts.summary: An enclosed intelligence report in another hand: Grenier's intrigue in clear, then in cipher advice that the ships be well guarded with two or three pinnaces in the channel, and news that a Jesuit (surname read Bastune?) has been sent post into Italy. No sign-level transcription exists.

texts.label: R8485-R8487, Lord Cobham to [Walsingham], Ostend, 20 Mar 1587/8 (ff. 71v-72v)
texts.summary: Cobham reports new companies at Oudenburg and stone and fagots coming by water from Eeclo, suspects an attempt on Ostend and asks to be removed to a safer place; he would think himself unhappy to be a means to conclude an irreligious peace, and argues against handing the prisoners Pigot and Barney over to the States. No sign-level transcription exists.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. R8485 and R8486, the two full pages of the letter, read as English sentences with a few ellipses; R8487 is the end of the letter with three short cipher runs and holes ("hath assured means to a special service, ... being ... as I wrote unto you"), a small share of the document; its holes are listed as gaps.

prior.where: DECODE lists the records as partially/non-decrypted; no decipherment on the leaves; CSP Foreign 1588 calendars other Cobham letters but not these
